name: Riverton Dynamo

location.about: A city of about 330,000 on a wide bend of the river: lace, then bicycles, then electrical engineering - the Hollins Brothers' dynamo works, where the club began, made the generators that lit half of Victorian England.

colours.story: Cerise and white - the colour of the copper windings in the dynamos, glowing when they were tested, and the white of the works' overalls.

away.shirt: slate grey with a cerise lightning flash

rivals.why: the Midlands' two European champions - Stonecross's two to Riverton's one, and they never let Riverton forget it
the town across the river - a dozen bridges and one long grudge, since 1884

history.title: The works team
history.text: Founded in 1879 by workers at Hollins Brothers' dynamo works. The Founders' Cup in 1894, 1895 and 1905; Second Division champions in 1901; second in 1907, and champions in 1912 and 1914.

history.title: Up and down the river
history.text: Champions again in 1922 - and relegated a few years later, back as Second Division champions in 1928. Second in 1934, the Founders' Cup in 1932 and 1957.

history.title: The lean years
history.text: Second in 1965 and 1970, but no trophy until the Charter Cup in 1983. Twice relegated, twice Second Division champions (1986 and 1992).

history.title: The Sparks fly
history.text: The Charter Cup in 1997 and second in the league, the Founders' Cup in 1999 and 2000, champions in 2002 - and in 2010 the Treble: the title, the Founders' Cup and the Charter Cup.

history.title: The strangest season
history.text: In the spring of 2011 Riverton won the Crown of Europe - and were relegated from the Premier Division in the same month, the cost of the European run. That December they won the Intercontinental Cup as a Second Division club.

history.title: Back again
history.text: Promoted as runners-up in 2012 and a top-division club ever since; Founders' Cup finalists in 2009 and 2025.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1912 = 1911-12).

legends.name: Arthur Hollins
legends.note: Owner of the dynamo works; the club played on his works' ground until 1902.

legends.name: Sid Kemp
legends.note: 247 goals - the club record, and all three of the early titles.

legends.name: Henrik Solberg
legends.note: The Treble, the Crown of Europe, the Intercontinental Cup - and the relegation in between.

legends.name: Danny Achterberg
legends.note: Scored the winner in the 2011 Crown of Europe final.

records.attendance: 58,700 v Darnford Albion, League, 1947 (Powerhouse Lane, before seating)

badge.about: The dynamo's lightning bolt and the river's bend; one star for the Crown of Europe. Motto 'Lux Ex Labore' - light from work.
badge.design: A cerise shield with a white border. In the centre a white lightning bolt striking down across a white wavy river. A small white star above the shield. 'RIVERTON DYNAMO' arched above the shield in cerise capitals, and a white ribbon beneath reading 'LUX EX LABORE' in cerise, with '1879' on the ribbon's ends.

ground.name: Powerhouse Lane

stands.name: Hollins Stand
stands.features: the main stand: tunnel, dugouts, boxes, built with the 2002 title money

stands.name: Turbine End
stands.features: the home end - two tiers in cerise seats; the old turbine hall of the works, now flats, behind it

stands.name: River Stand
stands.features: two tiers backing onto the river towpath; the next to be rebuilt

stands.name: Bridge End
stands.features: away fans; built during the season in the Second Division

ground.corners: the western corners filled; the eastern ones open
ground.surroundings: the wide river bending past the east stand, a dozen bridges, the brick turbine hall of the old dynamo works turned into flats, cooling towers far off on the skyline
ground.atmosphere: a big, loud city ground - and every visit from Darnford is a war

for_the_engine.notes: a city ground by the river
